draft.title: Technology and jobs
card: Technology such as machines, robots and artificial intelligence can do some tasks faster or more cheaply than people. This is called automation. Some jobs shrink or disappear as a result, such as checkout work when self-serve machines are used.
Technology also creates new jobs. People are needed to design, build, run and fix it, in areas such as software and data.
The jobs lost and the jobs created often need different skills. A checkout worker may not have the skills for a software job straight away.
Because technology keeps changing, workers may need to learn new skills.
draft.remember: Automation can remove some jobs and create others, so workers may need to learn new skills.

a.q: A supermarket in Melbourne adds self-serve machines at its checkouts and now needs fewer checkout staff. What does this show about automation and jobs?
opts: Automation can add more checkout jobs
Automation can make old skills last longer
Automation can keep the number of jobs the same
a.why: Self-serve machines do work that checkout staff once did, so the store needs fewer of them. Adding checkout jobs is tempting because technology does create jobs, but the new jobs are in areas such as software and data, not checkout work.
a.clue: Look at what happened to the number of checkout staff.

b.q: A Geelong bank uses an artificial intelligence app that handles many customer requests. It hires more data analysts to run the app and needs fewer tellers. What will most help a teller who wants to move into the new work?
opts: Learn new skills, such as working with data
Keep teller skills, as they suit data jobs
Learn more teller skills, such as handling cash
Wait, as the app will create more teller jobs
b.why: The new jobs need different skills from teller work, so the teller may need training or study in skills such as working with data. Keeping teller skills is tempting, but the jobs lost and the jobs created often need different skills.
b.clue: Do the old jobs and the new jobs need the same skills?

b.best: Learn new skills, such as working with data
